_about: Lane C (this lane runs second under that name; the prior agent's Lane C handoff covered these houses). Roy Morgan final pre-election waves for 2013, 2016, 2019 and 2022 with whatever demographic breakdowns the sources print. 2013 comes from the full multi-mode demographic release (finding 5169) saved verbatim as wayback HTML/text + 34 parsed tables. 2016: Morgan's own historical tables (repo mirror) prove their last 2016 wave was May 21/22 & 28/29 (finding 6831) — Morgan ran NO June 2016 wave. 2019: final face-to-face wave (finding 7975) from the ABIX mirror, exact-match with Wikipedia's table. 2022: final release 8981 (national only, live roymorgan.com) plus the penultimate week 8977 (state 2PPs in prose, live).

waves.finding: Roy Morgan finding No. 5169 ("L-NP set to win Federal Election as ALP primary vote collapses")
waves.method: multi-mode (SMS, Online and telephone interviewing) over three nights; Australian electors 18+
waves.note: ANALYSIS BY STATE tables print each cell once as 'vs 2010 Federal Election' tables (alp2/lnp2 here) and again as 4-week trend tables whose Sep 4-6 column differs slightly (trend2pp kept verbatim alongside). Gender exists ONLY as prose 2PP: 'Analysis by Gender shows Women now favouring the L-NP (51.5%) cf. ALP (48.5%) ... Men favouring the L-NP (55.5%) cf. ALP (44.5%)'. No gender primaries printed.

waves.finding: Roy Morgan finding 6831 ("Election now too close to call: ALP 51% cf. L-NP 49%. Minor Parties 'won' last night's Leaders' debate.") — Morgan's LAST 2016 wave; published 30 May 2016
waves.method: multi-mode via face-to-face and SMS interviewing over the last two weekends; Australian electors 18+
waves.tppResp: headline 51/49 is respondent-allocated ('allocated preferences based on how people say they will vote'); previous-election-flow basis prints ALP 51.5 / L-NP 48.5
waves.note: Full release re-fetched from Wayback after IA recovered (capture 20160531110325). National primaries verbatim from the release: L-NP 37.5 (up 1), ALP 32.5 (down 0.5), Greens 13 (down 2.5), NXT 5 (unchanged), Katter's Australian Party 1 (up 0.5), Palmer United 0 (unchanged), Independents/Others 11 (up 1.5). Only SA gets printed primaries ('Liberals (31%), NXT (26.5%) and the ALP (25%) with support for the Greens (8.5%) and Independent/Others (9%)'); all other state/age/gender splits are 2PP-only prose. NOT an election-eve wave: Morgan's tables show the next reading after this wave is the 2 July 2016 election result itself.

waves.finding: Roy Morgan finding 7975 ("ALP regains initiative with a week to go: ALP 52% cf. L-NP 48%") — final Morgan VI wave of the 2019 campaign; published 14 May 2019 per Morgan's own finding page (the ABIX mirror cross-posted 13 May its time)
waves.method: face-to-face interviewing, representative cross-section of Australian electors 18+
waves.note: Figures verified against BOTH the ABIX mirror and Morgan's own original release page (Wayback capture 20190516002222, re-fetched after IA recovered): identical, and the original likewise carries NO state/age/gender analysis — this was a slim release. Wikipedia's 2019 table carries identical figures (fieldwork 10-12 May; Morgan's original says only 'concluding on the weekend'). Preference basis: respondent's stated preferences. Follow-up special SMS poll (finding 7980, published 17 May 2019) asked only who would WIN: 66% ALP / 34% L-NP nationally — by supporter (ALP 81%, L-NP 53% for own side, Greens 84% ALP, Independents/Others 64.5% ALP) and by age (18-24: 80, 25-34: 74.5, 35-49: 65, 50-64: 61.5, 65+: 59 expecting an ALP win) — expectations only, no voting intention.

waves.finding: Roy Morgan finding 8977 ("ALP 53% leads the L-NP 47% and set to win the Election...") — penultimate week
waves.method: telephone and online interviewing of Australian electors 18+
waves.note: State figures are 2PP-only (2019-election-flow basis), printed in prose. 'oth' = printed 'Other Parties' 5%; 'ind' = printed 'Independents' 9% (release's umbrella: minor parties and independents 32%).

waves.finding: Roy Morgan finding 8981 ("ALP retains lead over the L-NP in the final week and set to win the Federal Election") — THE FINAL pre-election release; published Friday 20 May 2022
waves.method: Roy Morgan Single Source weekly tracking, 'interviewing throughout this week'; release prints no wave n (chart caption: average interviews per fortnight n=2,000, May 2019-May 2022)
waves.note: National figures only — the final-week release carries NO state/age/gender splits. Headline tpp is the 2019-election-flows basis; respondent-allocated preferences produce ALP 56.5 / L-NP 43.5 (both printed). PDF (8981-Federal-Voting-Election-Summary-May-20-2022.pdf) is prose-identical; its only charts are national + female + male 2PP trend charts (figures only as image lines, no printed endpoints).

notes: PUP KEYING (2013): the lane brief asked PUP be treated as inside oth with onp:null. The source PRINTS Palmer United Party as its own column, separate from 'Ind./Other', so for verbatim fidelity PUP is filed as its own 'pup' key (same pattern as the 'uap'/'nxt' keys used here and by the Newspoll lane); merge pup+oth downstream if a 4-party schema is needed. onp:null — One Nation was not in the field in 2013 (its 2013-era vote was inside Ind./Other).

Every 2013 state/city/age row sums to exactly 100 with the five printed columns; national sum 100. 2016 wave sums 100 (ONP printed 'n/a' → null). 2019 wave sums 100. 2022 waves sum 100 (34+34+13+4+1+5+9). No row exceeded 100.5.

L-NP PARENTHETICAL in 2013/2016 tables: 'L-NP 44 (3)' prints a bracketed second figure. In 2016 Morgan's own table header context (NXT column era) and the era's Morgan conventions this is the National-party component; in the 2013 release its definition is not restated on the page — filed as 'lnpParen' information only via this note: NSW (5.5), VIC (2), QLD (0.5), WA (5), SA (1), national (3), CapCities (0.5), Country (7); 2016 May 21/22&28/29 wave: (3.5). Do not treat as a party share.

2013 DUAL 2PP FORMS: each state's 2PP appears twice — the 'vs 2010 election' single table (filed as alp2/lnp2) and the 4-week trend table Sep 4-6 column (filed as trend2pp). Example NSW 48.5/51.5 vs 47/53. Both forms printed in the same release; no reconciliation attempted.

2016 MORGAN GAP RESOLVED: handoff expected an SMS poll ~1 Jul 2016 (L-NP 50.5). Disproven by Morgan's own historical tables (last wave May 21/22 & 28/29, then the election), the ABIX release index (consumer-confidence posts but no federal VI release 25 Jun-4 Jul 2016), Poll Bludger's 1 Jul 2016 final-roundup (which lists 'final results from Newspoll, Galaxy, ReachTEL, Ipsos and Essential Research' — no Morgan), and Wikipedia's 2016 table. The 'L-NP 50.5' memory belongs to the final Newspoll (50.5-49.5 Coalition). Live roymorgan.com does not serve pre-2021 findings (5169 and 7980 slugs both 404 live — saved as src/morgan/2019-sms-7980-live-404.html); all legacy-release content here therefore comes via Wayback captures (IA was 'Temporarily Offline' most of the pass, recovered near the end and yielded 6831 + 7975).
2022 GENDER: female/male 2PP trend charts exist only as images inside findings 8977/8981 (no printed endpoint figures) — not transcribed (pixel-reading a trend line would invent numbers).
2022 8981 fieldwork: exact dates/n not printed ('Roy Morgan continued interviewing throughout this week'); date filed as the 20 May 2022 publication date with dateStart null.
gaps: 2013-09-07: NOTHING missing from the release itself (full demographic pack captured).

2016-07-02: any June 2016 Morgan wave — none exists (see notes; the expected ~1 Jul SMS poll is a false memory of the final Newspoll). The 6831 release itself is now fully captured (state/gender/age 2PPs filed); remaining unfilled cells are those the release never printed (non-SA state primaries, age/gender primaries).

2019-05-18: nothing further — Morgan's own original release of 7975 (captured) carries no demographic analysis beyond what is filed. Probed and ruled out: live roymorgan.com legacy slugs (404); ABIX index complete May 12-21 2019 (only 7975 + the 7980 expectations SMS exist from Morgan that fortnight); Wikipedia contradictory-slug candidates 7952/7966/7968 are earlier May waves, not finals.
2022-05-21: printed state/age figures for the FINAL week (8981) do not exist in the release (national only); gender 2PP exists only as chart images.
